issues.display_title: Issue #1775: [Editor] Integrate Angular Signals with undo-redo history
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Make undo/redo restore serializable editor state through the Signals store while Babylon.js remains an imperative projection of the restored snapshot.

Scope

  • Define the serializable snapshot boundary for artworks, ordinary objects, text walls, exhibition settings, and camera data.
  • Restore the domain snapshot first, then reconcile the Babylon scene from that restored data.
  • Expose undo/redo availability and in-progress state as derived or readonly Signals.
  • Ensure selection and active controls are reconciled after a restore.
  • Keep history entries free of Babylon.js runtime objects.
  • Preserve existing debounce, invalid-state cleanup, and save-history behavior unless a change is required for correctness.
  • Add tests covering undo, redo, branch truncation after a new edit, and selection reconciliation.

Out of scope

  • Collaborative editing or event sourcing.
  • Persisting history across browser sessions.
  • Replacing Babylon.js rendering.

Acceptance criteria

  • Undo and redo restore matching serializable editor and Babylon scene state.
  • Undo/redo buttons expose correct enabled and busy states.
  • A new edit after undo removes the stale redo branch.
  • History snapshots contain no Babylon.js runtime objects.
  • Existing save and validation workflows remain unchanged.
  • Focused tests and the required development build pass.

QA Tester Summary — Issue #1775

Verdict: PASS — no coding defect found in the reviewed undo/redo Signals history flow.

Suite: qa_testing/tests/e2e/visual/issue_1775_editor_undo_redo_history.spec.ts (Playwright, rerunnable white/gray/black-box source-contract suite)

Test summary

# Method Scenario Expected result Confusion matrix Result
1 White box Serializable Signals history boundary Snapshots contain editor domain data only; Babylon runtime values are rejected TP PASS
2 Gray box Restore sequencing Domain snapshot is applied before settings and Babylon artwork/text/object reconciliation TP PASS
3 Gray box Selection reconciliation Only valid, non-deleted domain selections are restored after projection TP PASS
4 Black box Real undo/redo controls Unsaved title edit enables Undo; Undo restores title and enables Redo; Redo restores edited title TP PASS
5 Black box Redo branch truncation A new edit after Undo disables/removes the stale redo branch TN PASS
6 Regression guard Save/publish safety Temporary real-data edits were discarded by reload without Save or Publish TN PASS

Code review

Area Review result
Snapshot boundary EditorSessionStore normalizes JSON-safe artwork, ordinary object, text, exhibition, camera, and validity data; no Babylon runtime types are retained.
Restore behavior EditorService restores domain data, reconciles settings, projects Babylon entities, then restores only existing selections.
Derived UI state canUndo, canRedo, and restore-busy state are readonly computed Signals; the UI shows the matching spinner/disabled state.
Branch handling commitHistory() slices history at the active index before adding a new snapshot, removing stale redo entries.
Focused coverage Existing store and editor unit contracts cover clone safety, rollback, selection reconciliation, invalid runtime values, undo/redo, and branch truncation.

issues.display_title: Issue #1776: [Editor] Extract and clean up Babylon runtime lifecycle
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Separate Babylon.js runtime ownership from Angular application state and guarantee cleanup when the editor session ends.

Scope

  • Introduce a focused runtime service responsible for Engine, Scene, canvas, render loop, runtime nodes, and Babylon observables.
  • Define explicit initialization and disposal methods.
  • Stop the render loop and dispose scene/engine resources on editor teardown.
  • Remove registered window/document listeners, timers, and Babylon observable callbacks owned by the runtime.
  • Scope runtime ownership to the editor route/session where dependency constraints allow.
  • Keep serializable editor data in EditorSessionStore, not in the runtime service.
  • Add lifecycle tests using test doubles for initialization and idempotent disposal.

Out of scope

  • Visual changes to the editor.
  • Changing persisted exhibition data.
  • Rewriting individual Babylon editing operations unrelated to lifecycle ownership.

Acceptance criteria

  • Entering the editor creates one runtime session.
  • Leaving the editor stops rendering and disposes owned resources.
  • Re-entering the editor does not duplicate listeners or render loops.
  • Disposal is safe when initialization is partial or called more than once.
  • Babylon objects do not enter the Signals store.
  • Lifecycle tests and the required development build pass.

QA Tester Summary — Issue #1776

Verdict: PASS — no coding defect found in the reviewed Babylon runtime lifecycle.

Suite: qa_testing/tests/e2e/visual/issue_1776_editor_runtime_lifecycle.spec.ts (Playwright, rerunnable white/gray/black-box source-contract suite)

Real-site environment: Dev https://dev.villume.com/editor/d4bb931a-782c-47ca-807b-dbee0b74af5a · authenticated QA gallery qa test mix · 13 Aug 2026

Test summary

# Method Scenario Expected result Confusion matrix Result
1 White box Runtime ownership One focused service owns canvas, engine, scene, render loop, nodes, layers, and cleanup handles TP PASS
2 Gray box Explicit teardown Component destroy disposes runtime before detaching bridge and resets editor session state TP PASS
3 Gray box Listener/observable/timer cleanup Runtime registers removal/clear callbacks and safely disposes special resources before scene/engine TP PASS
4 Black box Real editor entry One canvas/editor runtime surface is present after entering the QA gallery editor TP PASS
5 Black box Leave and re-entry Leaving removes the editor canvas; re-entry returns to exactly one canvas with no duplicate editor surface TN PASS
6 Regression guard Partial/repeated disposal Focused lifecycle contracts cover partial initialization, repeated disposal, stale callbacks, and fresh next session TN PASS

Code review

Area Review result
Runtime scope EditorRuntimeService is route-provided for editor/:id, creating session-scoped runtime ownership.
Initialization initialize() creates exactly one active session and rolls back through dispose() if scene initialization fails.
Disposal Registered event listeners, Babylon observers, timers, intervals, camera controls, render loop, special resources, scene, and engine are cleaned in teardown order.
Re-entry protection Session tokens guard late callbacks after disposal, and a new session can initialize after a prior disposal.
Signals boundary EditorSessionStore remains free of Babylon Engine, Scene, Mesh, and Vector3 runtime types.

issues.display_title: Issue #1777: [Editor] Optimize Angular-Babylon change detection boundary
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Prevent the Babylon render loop and high-frequency pointer/camera work from triggering unnecessary Angular change detection.

Scope

  • Run the Babylon render loop and continuous runtime callbacks outside Angular's zone.
  • Re-enter Angular only when an observable UI state actually changes.
  • Keep live mesh, camera, and gizmo transforms inside Babylon during pointer movement.
  • Commit serializable transform state to Angular Signals at operation boundaries such as drag end, input commit, or undo/redo completion.
  • Throttle any genuinely required live UI readout to at most once per animation frame.
  • Add instrumentation or focused tests that verify state commits are bounded and behavior is preserved.

Out of scope

  • Changing rendering quality or Babylon optimization settings.
  • Replacing Zone.js application-wide.
  • Redesigning editor controls.

Acceptance criteria

  • The render loop executes outside Angular change detection.
  • Dragging and camera movement remain responsive and visually unchanged.
  • Persisted transform state is committed when an operation completes.
  • No Signal is updated on every render frame without a documented UI requirement.
  • Selection, validation, and save state still update the UI.
  • Focused tests and the required development build pass.

QA Tester Summary — Issue #1777

Verdict: PASS — no coding defect found in the reviewed Angular/Babylon change-detection boundary.

Suite: qa_testing/tests/e2e/visual/issue_1777_editor_change_detection_boundary.spec.ts (Playwright, rerunnable white/gray/black-box source-contract suite)

Real-site environment: Dev https://dev.villume.com/editor/d4bb931a-782c-47ca-807b-dbee0b74af5a · authenticated QA gallery qa test mix · 13 Aug 2026

Test summary

# Method Scenario Expected result Confusion matrix Result
1 White box Render-loop boundary Babylon render registration and every frame execute outside Angular TP PASS
2 Gray box Continuous pointer/camera work Pointer movement, per-frame gizmo transforms, and camera control use outside-Angular runtime APIs TP PASS
3 Gray box Commit boundary Angular is re-entered on pointer-up, pointer tap, and gizmo drag-end where UI/domain state must commit TP PASS
4 Black box Real editor responsiveness smoke Canvas stayed rendered through pointer movement; one explicit title input commit updated the UI and enabled Undo TP PASS
5 Black box State commit guard No persisted change was made: temporary title commit was discarded through reload without Save/Publish TN PASS
6 Regression guard Bounded zone-entry contracts Focused specs assert movement remains outside Angular and drag-end/tap re-enter once TN PASS

Code review

Area Review result
Render loop EditorRuntimeService.startRendering() wraps registration and render frames in runOutsideAngular().
Pointer movement Drag and main-pointer observers use addObserverOutsideAngular(); the high-frequency move handlers do not re-enter Angular.
Gizmo transforms Per-frame onBeforeRenderObservable work is outside Angular; only drag-end re-enters to finalize state and log activity.
UI/state boundaries Pointer-up, pointer tap, drag end, explicit input commits, and undo/redo completion are controlled boundaries for state/UI changes.
Signal protection notifyEntityDataChanged() is called from transform commit paths, not from the runtime render-loop callback.

issues.display_title: Issue #1788: [Styles] Unify the primary button on design tokens and drop the remote owl-carousel CSS
issues.main_description_html:
Context

The editor revamp (#1756 and follow-ups) moved the editor onto the oklch design tokens, but the shared button foundation underneath it was never migrated. .btn.btn-primary in src/assets/scss/bootstrap/_button.scss still resolved through Bootstrap's button-variant($color-primary, …), and $color-primary is the legacy yellow #FFDA16.

Every token-based surface therefore had to retone the primary button back to indigo in its own file. Twenty-five near-identical blocks had accumulated across 23 files — dialog partials, layouts, and page components — most of them carrying !important. The compiled styles.css shipped 28 separate .btn-primary rules. Any new surface that forgot its override rendered a yellow button, and media-support.component.html had resorted to borrowing two unrelated dialogs' style classes (styleClass="add-artworks edit-frame media-support") purely to inherit one of those overrides.

Separately, src/styles.scss carried @import 'https://assets.villume.com/DEV/assets/plugins/owl-carousel/owl.carousel.min.css'. Sass leaves an absolute-URL @import alone, so it landed verbatim on line 2 of the built styles.css as a render-blocking request to a third-party host — pointing at a /DEV/ asset path in production builds. Owl carousel itself is dead: no .owl-* markup anywhere in src, no owlCarousel() call, and the pricing page's horizontal drag is hand-rolled in _dragItemPrice(). about.component.spec.ts already asserts the page no longer uses it.

Scope

Primary button:

  • Rewrite .btn.btn-primary in bootstrap/_button.scss on var(--primary) / var(--primary-foreground) / var(--halo), adopting the shadow treatment already used by the majority of the retone blocks.
  • Out-specify Bootstrap's generated .btn-primary:hover (0,2,0) and .btn-primary:not(:disabled):not(.disabled):active (0,3,0) so the base wins without !important.
  • Preserve the existing border: 0 geometry so no button changes size.
  • Delete every override block that only restated the base colour treatment.
  • Keep blocks that add geometry, and keep the distinct "raised" treatment (inset highlight + layered shadow + translateY(-1px)) pending a design decision — see follow-ups.
  • Fix the two defects the consolidation exposes:
    • notifications-setting.component.scss forced $color-primary !important with a grey hover, which would leave it the only non-indigo primary button in the app.
    • primeNg/_table.scss pinned the invoice button label to $color-dark1 (#171717) for the old yellow fill; near-black on the indigo fill fails contrast.

Remote stylesheet:

  • Remove the owl-carousel @import from src/styles.scss.
  • Remove the owl-carousel entry from PricingComponent's loadScripts() call, keeping jQuery and matchHeight, which runMatchHeight() still needs.
  • Add a guard so a remote @import cannot silently return.

Note: $color-primary itself cannot simply become var(--primary). It feeds the $theme-colors map and rgba($color-primary, .1), and Sass colour functions require a static colour — a custom property is a compile error. The fix has to land at the output rule, not the variable.

Acceptance criteria

  • .btn.btn-primary is the only place that defines the primary button's colour.
  • No .btn-primary override remains that only restates background, colour, or shadow.
  • No new !important is introduced.
  • .btn-primary rule count in the built styles.css drops from 28 to 12 (the remainder being Bootstrap's inert generated rules and the invoice button's geometry).
  • No primary button renders yellow anywhere in the app.
  • The invoice table button's label meets contrast on the indigo fill.
  • The built styles.css contains zero @import statements.
  • No /DEV/ asset path is referenced from a production build.
  • A test fails if a remote @import is reintroduced into src/styles.scss.
  • Angular development build succeeds.
  • ESLint and Prettier pass on the changed files.

Follow-ups

Mapped while auditing, deliberately out of scope here:

  • Seven primary buttons still use a second, "raised" treatment (sidemenu, profile/information, profile-setting, account-setting, billing, reset-password, preview-exhibition). Not duplicated colour — a genuinely different style. Needs a design call: promote it to the base or retire it.
  • 73 #FFDA16 occurrences remain in the built CSS as non-button accents: progress bar, IntroJS tooltip, _global.scss links, spinners, the invoice .pending status, and the viewer.
  • common/_global.scss (23 $color-*, 0 tokens) and common/_viewer.scss (64 $color-*, 0 tokens) are unmigrated. This is why dark mode is incomplete — the built CSS contains exactly one .dark rule, the token block itself, so every hardcoded surface stays light when the theme is toggled.
  • Bootstrap still generates six yellow .btn-primary rules from $theme-colors. Inert today because every template uses class="btn btn-primary", but an element with btn-primary alone would render yellow.
  • The editor uses roughly 48 bespoke button classes, three spacing systems (legacy ml15-style helpers, Bootstrap mr-2, and token-based gap), three icon systems (vi-* font, pi-*, inline SVG), and three grid systems.
  • src/assets/ is excluded in .prettierignore as "Bundled third-party assets", but it holds ~9.1k lines of first-party design SCSS, so none of it is formatted.

QA Tester Summary — Issue #1788

Verdict: PASS — no coding defect found in the primary-button token consolidation and owl-carousel stylesheet removal.

Suite: qa_testing/tests/e2e/visual/issue_1788_primary_button_and_owl_cleanup.spec.ts (Playwright, rerunnable white/gray/black-box source-contract suite)

Real-site environment: Dev https://dev.villume.com/about · public marketing surface · 13 Aug 2026

Test summary

1 White box Shared primary foundation .btn.btn-primary uses primary/foreground/halo tokens, preserves border geometry, and wins hover/active without !important TP PASS
2 Gray box Consolidated consumers Invoice label and notification settings no longer force legacy yellow/dark primary-button colors TP PASS
3 Gray box Remote stylesheet removal styles.scss has no remote @import; pricing retains jQuery/matchHeight and hand-rolled drag without owl-carousel TN PASS
4 Black box Real primary CTA Public About CTA renders indigo with light foreground and token shadow TP PASS
5 Black box Real hover feedback Hover preserves indigo/foreground while adding brightness and the larger halo shadow TP PASS
6 Regression guard Runtime stylesheet scan Real page loaded with no owl-carousel stylesheet URL TN PASS

Code review

Base primary button Shared .btn.btn-primary uses var(--primary), var(--primary-foreground), and var(--halo) with existing border: 0 geometry.

issues.display_title: Issue #1790: [Editor] Unify form fields on a shared field-input mixin and retone PrimeNG off Aura's emerald
issues.main_description_html:
Context

The token migration reached buttons (#1788) but never reached form fields. Every surface that needed an input styled it locally, so the app shipped four different field languages at once:

  • Settings pages (profile-setting.component.scss .input/.textarea): var(--background) fill, 1px solid var(--input), calc(var(--radius) - 2px), hover tint, 0 0 0 3px var(--halo) focus ring.
  • Add Artworks / Media Support dialogs: transparent fill with a single border-bottom: 1px solid var(--muted-foreground) — plus [class.border-0]="…" bindings that removed the border the moment the field held a value, so the box changed shape while typing.
  • Editor sidebar (common/_editor.scss, input-number.component.scss, images.component.scss): var(--surface-tint) fill, var(--border), calc(var(--radius) - 6px), focus expressed as outline: 2px solid var(--ring) with a negative offset.
  • Publish panel and the Splash Screen dialog: a third mix of --surface-tint / --border / radius - 6px with per-field padding (8px 10.5px 6px 10.5px, padding: 3px 0px 0px 0px, …).

Two class-level defects fell out of the same split, and both are wider than the fields:

  1. Hover out-specifies focus. .p-select:not(.p-disabled):hover is (0,3,0) while .p-select.p-focus is (0,2,0), so moving the pointer over a focused control dropped its focus ring back to the hover tint. Same shape in input-date.component.scss and in the editor's title input.
  2. PrimeNG renders emerald. app.config.ts passes the stock Aura preset, whose primary is emerald. Every PrimeNG focus border, checkbox, slider and highlight is green unless a stylesheet fights it — which is why several partials carried !important retones, and why the exhibition-type select still showed a green border.

Three inputs also had no accessible name at all: the exhibition title, the text-definition field, and the artwork title in the dialogs relied on a wrapper pTooltip or on nothing.

Scope

Shared foundation:

  • Add a field-input($height, $padding-x, $font-size) mixin carrying the settings-page treatment: fill, border, radius, placeholder, hover tint, focus ring, .is-invalid.
  • Put it in common/_mixins.scss, not bootstrap/_input.scss, so component stylesheets can @import it without pulling CSS into their bundle.
  • Replace the local field blocks with @include field-input(...), passing a shorter height where the column is dense (34px editor rows, 30px number inputs) instead of redefining the look.

Surfaces migrated:

  • Add Artworks single/multi preview and Media Support title fields (primeNg/dialog/_artworks.scss), and drop the [class.border-0] bindings.
  • Editor sidebar: .content-input / .content-description fields, app-input-number (and its stepper), the year input.
  • Publish panel: description textarea, .input-affix, .copy-field / .btn-copy.
  • Splash Screen dialog: Header, Body, Button Text.
  • Exhibition title (editor.component.scss) and the text-definition field: heading at rest, field on hover/focus, so they look editable without turning the header into a permanent box.

Defects fixed alongside:

  • Guard the three hover rules with :not(:focus) / :not(.p-focus) so the focus ring survives the pointer.
  • Wrap Aura in definePreset with the indigo scale --primary already uses, so PrimeNG components stop rendering emerald at the source instead of per-component !important.
  • Delete .p-select.bg-dark (six !important declarations) — it existed only to retone the trigger away from that emerald, and the base .p-select already carries the shared treatment.
  • Remove the dead .content-slide .title-content .badge block; no markup matches it.
  • Add aria-label to the exhibition title, text definition, and artwork title inputs.
  • Tidy the text list row: symmetric padding, flex sizing instead of a fixed width: 270px that pushed the wrench icon out of the row on the narrow panel, and a collapsed border between rows.

Acceptance criteria

  • One mixin defines the field treatment; no surface restates fill + border + radius + focus for a plain input.
  • Settings, dialogs, editor sidebar, Publish, and Splash Screen fields share the same border, radius, hover, and focus ring.
  • No field changes its border or shape as a result of holding a value.
  • A focused input or select keeps its focus ring while the pointer is over it.
  • No PrimeNG component renders an emerald accent in any state.
  • No new !important is introduced; the .p-select.bg-dark block is gone.
  • Every text input in the editor has an accessible name.
  • The text list row keeps the wrench icon inside the row at the narrow panel width.

issues.display_title: Issue #1792: [Editor] Fix the colour picker against PrimeNG 21 markup and bring it onto the token system
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

The colour picker popover looks broken. It shows up in Setting → gallery colours, Text → colour, and the three colour fields in Edit Frame.

What you see when you open it:

  • A dark grey box sits around the colour gradient, inside an otherwise white popover — square corners poking over the popover's rounded ones.
  • The white marker on the hue strip is wider than the strip it slides along, so it hangs over both edges.
  • A wide empty gap to the right of the hue strip, making the popover much wider than its contents.
  • The hex row below is three loose pieces — swatch, a floating #, an input box — that don't line up with each other or with the fields used everywhere else in the editor.
  • The white dot marking the selected colour disappears when you drag it into the light corner of the gradient.

None of this is new styling gone wrong — it's the picker still being styled for an older version of PrimeNG, plus the library's default dark theme for this component showing through where our own popover was supposed to take over.

What it should look like

One clean popover on the app's surface: gradient and hue strip sitting directly on it, no dark box, no gap, rounded to match everything else. Below it, a single hex field styled like the rest of the editor's inputs, then the recent colours row.

Scope

  • Take the picker off the library's dark defaults so our popover is the only card.
  • Size the panel to its contents — no leftover space, no negative margins holding the layout together.
  • Fix the hue marker so it fits the strip, and make the gradient marker visible on light colours.
  • Rebuild the hex row as one field, matching the shared input styling from #1790.
  • Recent colours row: even spacing, hover feedback.

Accessibility

  • The hex input has no label for screen readers.
  • The colour swatch, the add-to-recents button and the recent swatches show nothing when focused by keyboard.

Note for whoever picks this up

The gradient and hue strip must stay 150px. PrimeNG hardcodes that number when it converts a click position into a colour — resize them and the markers stop matching the colour you picked, with nothing in the console to tell you.

Out of scope

Recent-colour swatches stay small (18px), under the recommended touch target. This is a dense desktop sidebar and the full gradient is always right above them. Worth revisiting if the editor ever ships to touch.

Verification

  • Open the picker in Setting, Text and Edit Frame — one card, no dark box, no dead space.
  • Drag across the gradient and the hue strip; the colour must follow the pointer exactly.
  • Check light and dark theme, and the disabled state.

issues.display_title: Issue #1794: [Editor] Polish the Edit Frame dialog: opening flash, spacing, dividers and hover states
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

The Edit Frame dialog (Artwork → frame icon) has a handful of rough edges that add up to a window that doesn't feel finished.

What you see:

  • Opening the dialog — before the content shows up, a thin white bar the width of the dialog slides in, then snaps to full size. It looks like something failed to load.
  • Between the two halves — the preview on the left and the settings on the right sit on the old page grid, and the space between them is patched together from paddings and negative margins. Hard to keep even, easy to knock out of line.
  • Bottom of the settings panel — the last part of the panel looks sheared off, most obviously under the colour picker when it's open.
  • Above the footer — two horizontal lines a few pixels apart, one slightly shorter than the other.
  • Save This Frame — sits on the same row as Done instead of next to the "Apply to all Artworks" checkbox, the way the original design had it.
  • The colour picker card — its shadow spreads out on every side and reads as a grey blob rather than the card being lifted off the panel.
  • Preview canvas — square corners, while everything around it in the dialog is rounded.
  • Saved frames, on hover — the thumbnail goes pale instead of dimming, and the two round buttons on top of it are hard to read: the edit one turns into a solid black disc and the icons are too big for the circles they sit in.
  • Save Frame popup — the "Frame Name" box is a grey fill with no border and no reaction when you hover or click into it, unlike every other input in the editor.

What it should look like

The dialog opens at its real size, straight into the content. Two evenly spaced halves, one divider above the footer, rounded preview, and hover states you can actually read. The Frame Name box behaves like the rest of the editor's fields.

Scope

  • Have the dialog's content ready before it animates in.
  • Put the two halves on a real grid with one spacing value, and drop the old column classes and the padding tricks that stood in for it.
  • Replace the custom scroll area in the settings panel with plain native scrolling, which is what was cutting off the bottom.
  • One divider above the footer, not two.
  • Move Save This Frame back beside the "Apply to all Artworks" checkbox, Done alone on the row below.
  • Soften the colour picker's shadow to the same recipe the other floating panels use.
  • Round the preview canvas.
  • Saved-frame hover: dim the thumbnail instead of washing it out, make the two buttons legible, size the icons to their circles, mark delete as the destructive one, and give both a visible keyboard focus ring.
  • Frame Name input onto the shared field styling from #1790 — same size as today, only the look changes.

Verification

  • Open Edit Frame a few times: no white bar, no size jump.
  • Scroll the settings panel to the bottom with the colour picker open — nothing cut off.
  • Hover a saved frame: thumbnail dims, both buttons readable, delete reads as destructive; tab to them and the focus ring shows.
  • Open Save Frame: the name box matches the editor's other inputs, same size as before.
  • Check light and dark.
